newsitem.title: USA: Clinton leads Dole by 15 percent in 3-state survey.
newsitem.headline: Clinton leads Dole by 15 percent in 3-state survey.

text.p: President Bill Clinton leads Republican Bob Dole by 15 percentage points in a sampling of voters across the key Midwestern states of Ohio, Michigan and Illinois, a Reuters poll said on Wednesday.

The poll of 1,325 likely voters in the three states, conducted by John Zogby Group International, found Clinton ahead of Dole by 47.3 percent to 32.2 percent. Reform Party nominee Ross Perot polled 4.4 percent.
The poll had a margin of error of plus or minus three percentage points.

Clinton's lead was widest in Michigan where he was 20.5 percentage points ahead of Dole. In Illinois, the president's advantage was 16 points. The race was closest in Ohio, where Clinton led by 13 points.

The three Midwestern states account for 61 electoral votes or 22 percent of the 270-vote-majority needed to win the presidency in the Electoral College, which formally chooses the president under the indirect U.S. election system. They are considered "swing" states -- moving back and forth between Democratic and Republican -- and have historically played a pivotal role in electing presidents.
